data.narrative:
Heliux is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Alex Craig and Victor Jakubiuk that has raised $4.7M to date. The relevant comp universe includes one public company (277810.KQ) and eight private peers in the robotics and manufacturing sector, including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI.

A stage-progression methodology is applicable to this valuation. Using the $4.7M raised as a proxy for current value and applying a typical seed-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.5x yields an implied valuation of $12M. A peer-median approach was not viable given insufficient data points; while ten same-sector peers exist, none of the narrow filters (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier) yielded the minimum three datapoints required for statistical reliability.

The triangulated analysis, based on the single applicable method, supports a valuation range of $10M to $14M, with a median of $12M. Key uncertainties center on the thinness of the comparable set and the absence of transaction data from closely staged peers. The seed-stage valuation rests primarily on standard expansion multiples rather than peer benchmarking, making actual fundraising outcomes and product traction validation critical inputs for a subsequent round valuation.
